Package neqsim.process.equipment.compressor

Class CompressorDeposit

java.lang.Object
neqsim.process.equipment.compressor.CompressorDeposit
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public class CompressorDeposit extends Object implements Serializable
Screening-level model of solid deposit (fouling) accumulation on a centrifugal compressor impeller and its effect on aerodynamic performance.

The model bridges deposit-generating flow-assurance calculations (elemental sulfur drop-out, salt carry-over, mineral scale, corrosion products, wax) and compressor performance. Any number of deposit mechanisms can be accumulated as a mass (kg) and the combined deposit is mapped to a fractional flow-area blockage and hence to a polytropic efficiency multiplier and a polytropic head multiplier.

Physical screening model

  1. Deposit volume: V = sum(mass_i / density_i) over all mechanisms.
  2. Film thickness on the foulable (wetted) impeller/inlet area: t = V / wettedArea.
  3. Flow-area blockage: b = min(t / passageHalfHeight, maxBlockage).
  4. Efficiency multiplier: m_eff = max(1 - kEff * b, minEff) — area reduction, added surface roughness and incidence losses compound (default kEff = 1.6).
  5. Head multiplier: m_head = max((1 - b)^headExponent, minHead) — throughput/area effect (default exponent 2).

The relations are screening-level. Coefficients (kEff, headExponent) are exposed so the model can be calibrated to measured degradation (for example a root-cause-analysis clean / partial / fully-degraded set of points).

Typical usage


 CompressorDeposit dep = CompressorDeposit.fromCompressor(compressor);
 dep.addDeposit(DepositMechanism.SULFUR_S8, 1.2); // kg from a sulfur drop-out study
 dep.addDeposit(DepositMechanism.SALT_NACL, 0.4); // kg from a salt carry-over study
 compressor.setDepositModel(dep); // degradation now applied in run()
 compressor.run();
 double effLoss = 1.0 - dep.getEfficiencyMultiplier();

    • sizeImpellerFromInletFlow

      public void sizeImpellerFromInletFlow(double inletVolumeFlow, double eyeAxialVelocity)
      Size the foulable impeller geometry from the inlet volumetric flow (screening).

      The impeller eye area is estimated as Q / eyeAxialVelocity; the foulable (wetted) area of the first stage is taken as six times the eye area (hub, shroud and blade surfaces) and the characteristic passage half-height as eyeDiameter / 12.

      Parameters:
      inletVolumeFlow - inlet actual volumetric flow in m3/s
      eyeAxialVelocity - impeller-eye axial velocity in m/s (typical 40-50 m/s)

    • depositMassForEfficiencyMultiplier

      public double depositMassForEfficiencyMultiplier(DepositMechanism mechanism, double targetEfficiencyMultiplier)
      Invert the efficiency model: find the total deposit mass of a single mechanism that yields a target efficiency multiplier, given the current geometry.

      Useful for calibration ("how much deposit is consistent with a measured efficiency drop?"). The current deposit inventory is not modified.

      Parameters:
      mechanism - deposit mechanism to solve for
      targetEfficiencyMultiplier - target efficiency multiplier (0-1)
      Returns:
      deposit mass in kg that yields the target multiplier (0 if geometry unset)
